changes: Added optional cross-platform cloud saves under Player & saves, using the same Google account for identity only, with no Google Drive permission. Signing in alone does not upload or restore progress; automatic syncing requires a separate opt-in.

Sync completed progression, review conflicting whole saves and restore backup history with local recovery copies. Graphics, audio and touch preferences stay on each device; unfinished runs, live co-op sessions and pending Expedition returns remain device-local.

Mac cloud login stays only in native memory, avoiding Keychain/Safe Storage access. A one-use localhost callback returns from the browser. Fully quitting requires connecting again; legacy encrypted login files and local game progress are left untouched.

Android Chrome uses an explicit Return to game tap targeting the installed app, with the pokebonk-offline custom scheme, a legacy alias and an alternate link. Temporary sign-in polling failures retry within the same attempt, with bounded backoff and safe error references.
Improved in-game updater status and download feedback. Downloads and installation remain explicit, verified native operations.
Preserved the co-op room when opening the original Pokémon selector and when returning from completed co-op results. Co-op peers must use matching app builds and connection modes.
Improved Android combat and collection text readability, restored missing task artwork, and retained normal earned progression, saves, application identity and signing identities.

Bundled all six original Series 2 Treasures banner glow layers, including Amethyst Cavern. Twelve look-frame URLs missing on the original site reuse their matching original prize-frame artwork offline, without granting cosmetics. Asset discovery now checks the original wheel/look catalogs rather than only literal paths.

Restored the complete original boss/elite status-icon set, including icons generated from status names during gameplay. Missing status artwork beneath boss HP bars in v1.2.0 is now included in the offline assets; preparation checks the finite status catalog rather than only literal icon references.

Co-op with multiple visible boss bars uses a compact two-column grid below the timer. The existing four display slots, enemy order, HP-number/percentage setting, phases and status warnings are retained. Solo and single-boss layouts are unchanged.

Adapted the original Expedition team panel to the existing LAN, STUN-only and direct-first TURN-fallback transports. Wild Valley and Safari Zone support two to four trainers, original loadout cards, chat, map selection and explicit Ready/Enter controls. Solo entry remains available.

Expedition discovery is filtered to the selected map. Find teammates and Duo/Trio/Squad use the same bounded native room controls as regular co-op; account friends, player trading, rankings and competitive prizes remain excluded.

Each trainer durably escrows their own equipment, route card and insurance before the shared start barrier. A canceled preparation restores that escrow. Original gifts and backpack rescues use local ownership receipts, duplicate suppression and acknowledged retries; rescued items return to their owner rather than becoming the rescuer's permanent equipment.

Once saved runs and deliverable item returns are complete, the existing room can return to its lobby for another Expedition. Temporary interruptions retain the current run; permanently departed players' undelivered returns remain in the save rather than being granted to somebody else.

Updated the bundled upstream game from 0.10.26 to 0.10.31 (mwv6wzyo), including the original Pokédex+ hub, collection and move-history tracking, engine/UI fixes and Expedition changes. Official account/chat/leaderboard services remain disconnected; original game data, art, credits and earned progression are retained.

The new Expedition wanted-loot preferences and Sort and stack action use local transactional saves. Wanted loot follows the original allowlist; sorting conserves quantities, locked stacks, gear and safe-pocket contents. The long preference modal is scrollable on short screens.
Refreshed all exposed public rental listings for the new upstream snapshot. Runtime rental data remains bundled and never requires the official API.

The save format and app identity remain unchanged. Older unfinished-run checkpoints are preserved and must be completed in their previous version until new-engine replay compatibility is established. Completed progression profiles remain importable.

Bundled all 1,104 publicly listed rental builds for 138 Pokémon, refreshed from online v0.10.31. Builds → Rental reuses the original browser and copy flow offline, preserves creator attribution and earned unlock requirements, and removes live account links and rental payouts. The snapshot is refreshed whenever a new upstream game version/build is integrated.
The Left to use HUD panel has a separate heading row, wrapping icon/count pairs and compact rounded corners so multi-row contents stay inside its background.

Shared graphics quality now limits the actual 3D rendering buffer on every platform. Battery Saver disables bloom and reduces internal resolution even with fixed/native output. While enabled, it selects and locks the FPS controls to 30; switching it off restores the previous FPS choice without changing saved quality preferences or UI sharpness.

Bundled five missing original status/seal icons, including the Fury Seal image, through a hash-checked image supplement. Corrected Cinnabar Island’s co-op map identifier to canela so its picker artwork and earned unlocks match the game catalog.

Restored the original co-op map picker, Normal/Hard/Nightmare selector and all five mode buttons: Classic, Survival, Relay, Daily Mutation and Boss Rush. Ordinary map/difficulty choices respect every teammate’s unlocks.

Daily Mutation resolves its original rules from the room’s shared rule time, and Boss Rush freezes the weekly boss lineup to that same room clock. Teammates retain the same settings, seed and ticket through recovery.

Find teammates controls random-match and Pick Rooms visibility. New rooms are code-only; switching discovery off keeps existing teammates connected. Duo, Trio and Squad enforce capacities of two, three and four players without kicking current members.

Android HP numbers under the player use white lettering with a thin shadow instead of the heavy text stroke that obscured digits on some tablet WebViews. Health-bar colors, sizing, shields and HP values are unchanged.

Android friendship-level numbers use a behind-text outline so the badge digits stay readable in the League header, Friendship panel, collection tiles and run results. Friendship levels, rewards and badge artwork are unchanged.

Added a bounded 90-second co-op recovery path for temporary LAN, STUN and TURN-fallback interruptions while the apps stay open. Private seat credentials reconnect the same players instead of joining a new room.

The existing run pauses during recovery and resumes only after the team’s synchronization barrier. Pokémon, roster, run ticket and local reward settlement are retained; no fresh run is minted by reconnecting.

A game-styled reconnect notice includes Give up. A permanent connection failure or the 90-second timeout automatically ends the attempt through the normal run results and local saving path. Failed writes keep the previous ticket/checkpoint; late reconnect packets cannot resume an abandoned attempt.
Desktop releases mouse capture during recovery so Give up is accessible. Force-closed apps and host migration are not part of this recovery path.

App updates stay in the game-styled modal from checking through download progress, verification, errors and installation handoff. App-controlled updater alerts no longer use native system message boxes.
Downloads display the actual percentage and transferred size against the signed release size. Hiding the modal does not stop the download; Check for updates reopens the current progress.
Install update is offered only after verification, and the downloaded file and save compatibility are checked again before opening it. Installation remains an explicit choice.

Android keeps its required system installation and permission confirmations. Desktop installers open after the game safely closes; portable/archive builds show their verified download and replacement instructions.

Added optional Internet co-op with STUN-only and direct-first TURN-fallback connection modes alongside offline LAN play. The entry and room screens show connection status without adding a gameplay overlay.
Find a random match joins a compatible open room. Pick Rooms lists available rooms without reserving seats or requesting TURN credentials until a player joins.
Join and share using four-character LAN codes or six-character Internet codes, with individual-character inputs, paste support and code copying.
Back, Esc and Android Back now ask before leaving a room. The confirmation buttons are centered; opening the Lab still preserves the room.
Improved Android native action routing and WebView-compatible Internet requests so room creation, discovery and joining use the same co-op flow as desktop.
Permanent TURN issuer and service administration credentials stay server-side. The game renderer remains isolated; compatible peers try direct connections before an authorized temporary relay.
Normal progression, existing saves, app identity and the Android signing certificate are preserved. Android build number advances to 12.

Room-to-Lab navigation no longer resets the online room URL. Desktop only closes LAN sessions for actual main-document navigation, not ordinary loading or in-page history changes. The homepage Co-op subtitle is now With friends.

Moved Find a match into its own card above How to play. Network selection and Personal Records filters now share the original leaderboard dropdown styling, map colors, selected-row highlight and animations, without menus being cropped by their panels.
Added Find a match for compatible open LAN rooms using bounded local discovery, with search feedback, cancellation and manual-invitation fallback. Full and in-progress rooms are not advertised.
Matched the homepage Survival / Endless mode and Co-op labels, with clearer icon-to-text spacing.

Added experimental 2–4-player LAN co-op for Classic / Viridian Forest / Normal, with native private-network pairing, in-room Pokémon changes and local progression. No internet matchmaking, STUN/TURN, leaderboards or online prizes.
Moved the online-style Co-op button below Endless and Relay into Game Modes. Reorganized the co-op entry into three desktop columns and removed its redundant Pokémon selector.
Fixed leaving a local room and immediately creating another: retired room callbacks can no longer close or adopt a newer room.

Check for updates now opens a game-styled loading dialog immediately, followed by clear version details for up-to-date apps, newer local test builds or connection/verification failures. Downloads and installation remain explicit native actions.
Centered the empty Personal Records messages in KOs, Survival and Time Attack, including the full records dialog and filtered empty results.
Android Automatic theme follows the device on startup, foreground activation and live light/dark changes. Explicit Light and Dark preferences are preserved; OEM automatic recoloring remains disabled.

Fixed tablet Expedition title, map labels, equipment names and reward text using behind-the-fill outlines rather than unsupported text-stroke paint order. Entry buttons now have a continuous rounded border, with the gold bevel inside it and an unclipped outer shadow.
Enabled the original solo Wild Valley and Safari Zone Expedition engines with local equipment, a safe pocket, insurance, seeded loot, extraction and defeat settlement.

Added Bill's local shop, inventory purchases/sales/recycling/repairs, daily contracts, a permanent earned Expedition Pass and My Extractions. Player trading, co-op, borrowed Pokémon, rivals, rankings and competitive prizes remain excluded.

Expedition loadouts are escrowed atomically with the run ticket. Duplicate settlements and claims cannot duplicate rewards. Interrupted raids preserve their last durable inventory checkpoint and require explicit defeat settlement, not a silent reset or free extraction.
Restored Expedition loot-filter settings. Existing profiles receive no automatic Pokémon or equipment unlocks.
Refreshed the pinned game source to 0.10.26, including the eleven new Maximum-form sprite sheets, Korean-name correction and upstream fixes from 0.10.24–0.10.26.

Added desktop window-state restoration, DPI-aware monitor/size selection, foreground keep-awake, native fullscreen, graphics diagnostics and restart-required alternate ANGLE backends. Auto remains the default; failed alternate launches restore Auto.

The original illustrated Guide opens once after reaching the homepage, never over either starter-selection screen. It follows the upstream 1.2-second delay and waits for other dialogs; preserved unfinished runs are never interrupted.

After finishing or skipping the first Guide, new players choose a local trainer name in a game-styled setup dialog. The name and completion marker save atomically, and existing custom names are preserved.
Android homepage logo outlines render behind the letters on older tablet WebViews. The animated shine inherits the same font metrics and letter spacing instead of appearing as offset duplicate text.

Startup waits for the actual menu BGM to be decoded and respects muted preferences. No loading-screen button is needed: after at most twelve seconds it continues automatically without music if audio is unavailable.
Removed Android's three-dot overlay and its reserved space. Native backup export/import, update checks and bug reporting now share the game-styled Player & saves dialog.

Android outlined titles use behind-the-fill shadow outlines rather than WebView-dependent text strokes; the app also disables OEM automatic darkening. New APKs use their own bundled runtime rather than a stale WebView HTTP cache.

Classic and Endless checkpoints from 0.10.20 and 0.10.23 were replayed in the new engine with their original tickets, balance, time and gold retained. Unknown unfinished-run builds are still preserved and rejected rather than reset.
The homepage dock is compact and slightly wider than the logo/version, with grouped upper-left controls, a taller personal-records table, and centered Relay/Game Modes artwork.
Added the offline creator beside Credits and the Android menu version, preserved the full Credits logo, and added starter-card confirmation spacing without increasing the screen height.
The player counter now uses the actual Play-screen catalog and ownership gate to show usable Pokémon.
New profiles start with 10,000 Stardust; loading or importing an existing save never changes its balance.
Restored the original illustrated Guide, excluding co-op, community, rankings and other unavailable online information.
Report a bug opens the project’s fixed GitHub issue form through trusted native code, without exposing renderer networking or uploading saves.
Android’s Player & saves header is full-bleed. Starter selection keeps roomy artwork when space permits, compacts only when needed, and gives all three Pokémon equal-height image panels.
Bundled the missing Clover Sweet event-reward icon discovered during offline checks, without altering earlier pristine captures.
Corrected homepage keyboard focus order and contained the Daily Mutation backdrop while keeping its Back control below the desktop title bar.
The Great Expedition replaces Practice in Game Modes as a clearly marked visual draft. Its local inventory/extraction backend is not implemented or enabled yet; no working gameplay is claimed.
Compact homepage controls leave more of the background visible, with an inline Personal Records table and Game Modes beside Endless and Relay.
The player row shows the actual Pokédex seen/total count; the extra OFFLINE · LOCAL SAVES label is removed.
Boss Rush and Lavender Tower restore the original challenge, pass and mission screens, with permanently available, locally earned rewards and no online leaderboard or competitive prizes.
Reward claims are atomic and cannot be collected twice. Earlier records-only event tickets retain their original rules and finished runs are not retroactively rewarded.
Daily Mutation has its original dedicated poster, rules and milestone rewards without the online ranking panel.
Player & saves includes a native-owned update check. Android’s app menu now uses the actual game fonts, theme and buttons instead of a system list.

status: Earlier local test build — not published
changes: Mewtwo Strikes Back and Lavender Tower are permanently available as offline challenges, without event prizes or leaderboards.
Daily Mutation runs locally, with earned progression and no server ranking.
Homepage layout follows the website-style Play, Endless, Relay, Event and Tasks buttons; Relay uses Pokémon portraits.
Personal Records has persistent KOs, Survival and Time Attack tables containing only this save’s results.
The OFFLINE version badge opens this bundled history and identifies the associated upstream game.

status: Earlier local test build — not published
changes: Updated the reviewed game payload from 0.10.20 to 0.10.23, preserving compatible Classic and Endless checkpoints.
Fixed tablet starter portraits and upgrade-card artwork, Android minimap scaling and the 30 FPS battery-saver cap.
Restyled the Android app menu and enlarged its launcher artwork; removed redundant fullscreen controls.
Restored desktop mouse-hover animations; closing the last macOS window now quits after pending saves finish.
Corrected Unicode normalization in macOS app/helper names to prevent startup crashes.
Restored normal Android screen edges and slightly reduced HUD/touch-control size.
Prepared the macOS, Windows, Linux and signed Android distributions.

status: Initial local build — not a public release
changes: Established the native Standard edition with normal progression rather than automatic unlocks.
Added atomic application-data saves, explicit backup import/export and signed native update discovery.
Bundled Classic, Endless, Relay and Practice without online accounts, multiplayer or game-server connections.
